_meta.indication: In conjunction with diet and exercise, for the treatment of adults with noncirrhotic nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (consistent with stages F2 to F3 fibrosis)

pivotal_trials.design: 54-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial of resmetirom 80 mg and 100 mg daily versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with metabolic risk factors and biopsy-proven noncirrhotic NASH with fibrosis stage 2 or 3 and a NAFLD Activity Score (NAS) of at least 4
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening of fibrosis, and at least one stage improvement in fibrosis without worsening of steatohepatitis, on Month 12 liver biopsy (histologic surrogate endpoints)
pivotal_trials.n: 888 patients randomized 1:1:1 (placebo n=294, REZDIFFRA 80 mg n=298, REZDIFFRA 100 mg n=296)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses achieved statistical significance on both histopathology endpoints. NASH resolution (Pathologist A): 13% placebo, 27% (80 mg, difference 14 [95% CI 8, 20]), 36% (100 mg, difference 23 [95% CI 16, 30]). Fibrosis improvement (Pathologist A): 15% placebo, 23% (80 mg, difference 8 [95% CI 2, 14]), 28% (100 mg, difference 13 [95% CI 7, 20]).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and higher than placebo): diarrhea, nausea, pruritus, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, and dizziness. Diarrhea EAIR 14/23/33 per 100 PY (placebo/80 mg/100 mg); nausea 9/18/15. Key warnings are hepatotoxicity and gallbladder-related adverse reactions (cholelithiasis, cholecystitis).
target_moa: Resmetirom is a partial agonist of the thyroid hormone receptor-beta (THR-beta); it produced 83.8% of the maximum response compared to T3 with an EC50 of 0.21 microM in an in vitro functional assay for THR-beta activation
modality: Small molecule (first-in-class new molecular entity, oral tablet)

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not convened for the review of this NDA

surrogate_endpoint.text: Histologic surrogate endpoints at Week 52 (resolution of NASH and improvement in fibrosis) considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit

citations.quote: This indication will be approved under accelerated approval based on improvement of NASH and fibrosis.

An interim analysis of surrogate endpoints at Week 52, which are considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in the target patient population, was conducted to support an accelerated approval and is the focus of this review.
The results of the histological surrogate endpoints considered to be reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit support demonstration of effectiveness for an accelerated approval action.

summary.text: Resmetirom received accelerated approval under 21 CFR part 314 subpart H based on histologic surrogate endpoints reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with a required confirmatory trial (MGL-3196-11) to verify clinical benefit. The application had Fast Track (2019), Breakthrough Therapy (2023), and Priority review designations.
